analysis:
Examined both primary analyses and independently checked the replayed patches, metadata and BASE/HEAD stop-sequence source against the canonical index and supplied T-041 definition. EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift:249–250 (HEAD patch) adds stopStringScope to request translation. EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift:14–31 (HEAD) uses that same scope to identify the terminating stop, while retaining the previous earliest-match behavior for unscoped requests. These changes are consistent with the reported final-output-only stopping intent, but the documentation excerpt itself was omitted from replay. No visible change establishes a regression in authorization, attestation, hop encryption, billing or cache isolation; none is inferred from missing implementations.

The two local questions converge on one unresolved cross-file contract: verify stopStringScope initialization and translation through EngineV2Translation, CBv2StopStringScope, native generation and event-pump holdback. In particular, StopSequence.swift:30 assumes scan.text is an exact prefix of the original decoded scalar stream. The supplied source cannot establish that contract or agreement between whole-output replay and incremental processing across split channel markers, Unicode and tool frames. Review final-output truncation, token-budget enforcement and cancellation when analysis-channel stops are ignored (A-001, TB-007, T-007, T-010).

The changed pins at libs/mlx:1, libs/mlx-swift:1 and libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 contain no dependency diffs. Their runtime, stop-processing and memory/cache effects require review, including preservation of T-041 authenticated cacheSalt scoping, encrypted storage and staging ownership. Replay omits four reviewed source units and supplies neither dependency implementations nor unchanged callers. These material coverage limits remain unresolved; an empty findings list is not security clearance.
